# venona ontology -- AI-industry instance. THE contract between research and graph.
#
# Generated file: the model's schema enums, the analyze extraction guide, the
# writer's predicate whitelist, the projector's filter, docs/graph-schema.md
# and the --entity-* tokens are all GENERATED from this. Edit here, bump
# `version`, rebuild.
#
# A data file rather than code because an enum enforces MEMBERSHIP but not
# MEANING: a whitelisted predicate used backwards ("$99M OTA AWARDED_TO
# Anduril") rots silently in a graph with no `domain`/`range` to reject it at
# load time. This file is that rejection.

version: 1

# ── the organisation family ──────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Three types, not one `Organization`. AI-industry press treats "who sells /
# funds it," "who studies / evaluates it," and "who regulates / convenes it"
# as different actors with different verbs -- a lab COMPETES_FOR nothing a
# regulator does, and a regulator REGULATES nothing a lab does. Splitting them
# is what makes "which companies compete with each other" and "which bodies
# regulate this model" separately queryable instead of both landing on one
# 400-entity bucket.

entity_types:
  Company:
    # color_slot indexes the --entity-slot-* palette; unique per type, 1..9.
    color_slot: 1
    prefix: company
    description: >-
      A commercial firm in the AI stack: a frontier lab, chipmaker, foundry,
      hyperscaler cloud, AI-native startup, or an investor funding any of
      those.
    guidance: >-
      Anything that sells, ships, or funds AI products -- including labs
      whose charter is nonprofit-adjacent (OpenAI's nonprofit-controlled
      capped-profit structure, Anthropic's PBC-plus-Trust structure) but that
      ship through a commercial operating entity: file the entity acting in
      the sentence as the Company, and reserve ResearchOrg for when an
      article is specifically about the nonprofit/governance side rather than
      the product. A renamed or restructured division is its own Company
      linked with PART_OF ("Meta Superintelligence Labs" is not "Meta AI"
      once the article treats the restructuring as real). Sovereign wealth
      vehicles (MGX, PIF, Mubadala) are Companies with org_type investor, not
      GovernmentBodies -- they write cheques and sit in cap tables the way
      Sequoia does, which is how the press treats them even though the money
      is state-owned. A single-product startup named identically to its
      product (Perplexity, Midjourney, Runway, DeepSeek) is the Company; the
      product of the same name is a Product -- see confusable_with.
    examples: [OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, TSMC, DeepSeek, Mistral AI, Thrive Capital, SoftBank Group]
    org_types: [lab, hyperscaler, chipmaker, foundry, startup, investor]
    # Perplexity, Midjourney, Runway and DeepSeek are all cases where the
    # company and its (only) product share one name with no textual signal
    # distinguishing "Perplexity raised a round" from "Perplexity shipped a
    # feature." NOT confusable with GovernmentBody: sovereign-fund status is
    # settled by fiat above (org_type: investor), not by an ambiguous
    # sentence, so there is no real blur to name there.
    confusable_with: [ResearchOrg, Product]

  GovernmentBody:
    color_slot: 2
    prefix: govt
    description: >-
      A state, intergovernmental, or standards arm with staff and a mandate
      to regulate, evaluate, approve, or fund AI on behalf of a public
      authority.
    guidance: >-
      Anything that approves, restricts, standardizes, or evaluates on
      government authority. Use the most specific body named -- "UK AI
      Security Institute," not "the UK government." A named coalition with a
      governing process but no shared staff (the International AI Safety
      Institute Network, launched from the Bletchley Summit process) still
      belongs here, the way NATO does in an alliance-heavy domain: connect
      its member institutes with PART_OF rather than inventing a membership
      predicate. The EU is a GovernmentBody (the European AI Office is its
      organ) even though "the US-China-EU AI race" is common framing --
      assert REGULATES or COMPETES_WITH about the body or country actually
      named in the sentence, not "Europe" generically.
    examples: [Cyberspace Administration of China, European AI Office, UK AI Security Institute, US FTC, NIST/CAISI, OECD.AI Policy Observatory]
    org_types: [regulator, standards_body, evaluator_institute, coalition, agency]
    confusable_with: []

  ResearchOrg:
    color_slot: 3
    prefix: research
    description: >-
      A body that studies, evaluates, or publishes open research rather than
      selling or regulating: a nonprofit lab, academic institute, third-party
      evaluator, or open-research collective.
    guidance: >-
      Non-commercial by construction, even when it ships models or holds
      paid contracts -- Ai2 publishing OLMo, or METR running commissioned
      evaluations, does not make either a Company, the same way an FFRDC
      holding a contract doesn't make it a prime. Use ResearchOrg for a
      frontier lab's nonprofit or research-only face specifically when the
      article is about governance rather than product (OpenAI's controlling
      nonprofit foundation, as distinct from OpenAI Global LLC the Company).
    examples: [METR, Epoch AI, Apollo Research, Allen Institute for AI, Stanford HAI, Mila, EleutherAI, MIRI]
    org_types: [nonprofit_lab, academic, evaluator, open_collective, think_tank]
    # Intergovernmental policy arms (OECD.AI) and government-adjacent
    # standards evaluators (NIST/CAISI, UK AISI) sit on a real boundary: is
    # a "policy observatory" GovernmentBody staff or ResearchOrg-style
    # analysis? The sentence rarely settles it, unlike the settled
    # Company/GovernmentBody question above.
    confusable_with: [GovernmentBody]

# NOT an entity: a PUBLISHER (TechCrunch, The Information, Import AI) is
# `documents.source_id` and becomes an entity only when an article is ABOUT
# the publication itself. An EVENT -- even a named recurring one like the
# Bletchley/Seoul/Paris AI Action Summit series -- has no single stable
# canonical surface across write-ups ("the Paris summit," "AI Action Summit
# 2025," "the third safety summit") and no relation in this file needs it as
# an endpoint; a claim ABOUT a summit is really a claim about the
# GovernmentBodies or Countries that attended or issued a declaration there.

  Product:
    color_slot: 4
    prefix: product
    description: >-
      A specific, named AI artifact someone builds: a model, a chip, a
      coding agent, an agent platform, a robot, or a benchmark.
    guidance: >-
      Concrete and nameable, with a canonical surface independent of who
      currently owns it. A model FAMILY name (Claude, Gemini 3, Llama 4) is
      the Product, not each numbered checkpoint or point release -- track
      version strings as an attribute of the assertion, not a new entity.
      Chips (Nvidia Rubin, TPU Ironwood), coding agents (Claude Code,
      Cursor, GitHub Copilot), enterprise agent platforms (Salesforce
      Agentforce, Palantir AIP, Amazon Bedrock), robots (Figure, Tesla
      Optimus), and benchmarks (SWE-bench, MMLU, ARC-AGI, Chatbot Arena) are
      all Products; product_type carries the distinction, the way
      platform_type would in a hardware-only domain. A named megaproject
      with sponsors and sites (Stargate) is a Product too, product_type
      infra_project -- it is a thing being built, not the org building it.
    examples: [Claude, ChatGPT (GPT-5.6), Gemini 3, Nvidia Rubin, Claude Code, Figure, SWE-bench (Verified), Stargate]
    product_types: [model, chip, software_platform, coding_agent, agent_platform, robot, benchmark, infra_project, media_tool]
    # A named technique/architecture (Technology) and the flagship product
    # that popularizes it sit on one boundary the sentence rarely settles --
    # is "MCP" the protocol (Technology) or the thing Anthropic shipped
    # (Product)? See Technology.confusable_with for the declaration.
    confusable_with: [Technology]

  Technology:
    color_slot: 5
    prefix: tech
    description: >-
      A capability, architecture, or training technique independent of who
      ships it.
    guidance: >-
      Use for methods and architectures, not the named artifact that
      implements them -- "mixture of experts" is a Technology; "DeepSeek V4"
      is a Product that IMPLEMENTS it. Training/alignment techniques (RLHF,
      DPO, GRPO, Constitutional AI), architectural patterns (MoE,
      retrieval-augmented generation, test-time compute), and research
      capability areas (interpretability, red-teaming) belong here, not as
      Products, even when a lab brands its version with a product-sounding
      name (Anthropic's "Constitutional AI").
    examples: [Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, Mixture of Experts, test-time compute, Constitutional AI, interpretability]
    confusable_with: []

  Person:
    color_slot: 6
    prefix: person
    description: A named individual in a professional AI-industry capacity.
    guidance: >-
      Only extract people whose role matters to the relationship being
      asserted -- a founder, a researcher who moved labs, a named executive
      -- not a quoted bystander. Several flagship model names double as
      ordinary first names (Claude) or as historical figures behind chip
      codenames (Grace Hopper behind Nvidia's "Grace"); these are different
      entities that happen to share a string with a Product, not the same
      thing filed twice, and confusable_with is deliberately empty here for
      exactly that reason -- see Product's guidance.
    examples: [Sam Altman, Jack Clark, Ilya Sutskever, Demis Hassabis]
    confusable_with: []

  Country:
    color_slot: 7
    prefix: country
    description: >-
      A sovereign state -- the top-level actor an organization belongs to,
      or a party to a geopolitical AI claim in its own right.
    guidance: >-
      States only. Not blocs: the EU is a GovernmentBody (see above), and
      export-control and "AI race" coverage that says "the US" or "China"
      without naming a specific agency should be asserted about the Country
      directly -- REGULATES and COMPETES_WITH both admit Country for exactly
      this framing, which is routine in this domain's press ("the US
      restricts advanced chip exports to China") in a way it rarely is
      elsewhere. Not regions ("the Gulf") or cities. An organization is
      BASED_IN its country, never PART_OF it.
    examples: [United States, China, France, United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates]
    confusable_with: []

predicates:
  # ── archetype coverage ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # adoption/use : org|Product --ADOPTS--> Product|Technology
  # competition  : Company|ResearchOrg|Product|Country --COMPETES_WITH--> same (symmetric)
  # composition  : Product|Technology --BUILDS_ON--> Product|Technology ;
  #                Company|ResearchOrg|Product --IMPLEMENTS--> Technology
  # funding      : Company|GovernmentBody --FUNDS--> Company|Product
  # production   : Company|ResearchOrg --PRODUCES--> Product        (anchor)
  # partnership  : org|Country --PARTNERS_WITH--> org|Country (symmetric)
  # regulation   : GovernmentBody|Country --REGULATES--> Company|Product|Technology|Country
  # membership   : GovernmentBody --PART_OF--> GovernmentBody (coalition),
  #                the same recursive edge that carries corporate/research
  #                hierarchy -- no separate MEMBER_OF, matching how the
  #                alliance case is handled in the exemplar domain.
  # COMPETES_FOR (bidding for a named Program) is dropped: this domain has no
  # Program-type entity -- AI-era "competing for" claims are market
  # competition (COMPETES_WITH) or adoption (ADOPTS: a customer choosing a
  # vendor), both already expressible, not bids against a named acquisition
  # effort the way defense-press COMPETES_FOR claims are.

  PART_OF:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: The subject is a constituent part of the object.
    guidance: >-
      Child --PART_OF--> parent, always. This is the recursive org chart:
      Meta Superintelligence Labs PART_OF Meta once a restructuring is
      treated as real by the article; UK AI Security Institute PART_OF the
      International AI Safety Institute Network, the way NATO's members
      connect to NATO. It crosses the three org types freely by design. A
      Product is never PART_OF anything and this is the commonest miss --
      "Claude Code is part of Anthropic's product line" is ordinary English
      naming the wrong edge; the org PRODUCES the product, and the loader
      rewrites this shape rather than dropping it (see rewrites). Countries
      are never a PART_OF object either -- an organization is BASED_IN its
      country.
    example: UK AI Security Institute --PART_OF--> International AI Safety Institute Network

  BASED_IN:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Country]
    # Small closed set (ISO-backed) that nearly every org in the graph
    # points at; leaving it in shortest-path search turns "how does Mistral
    # relate to DeepSeek" into "both BASED_IN a country," a true but useless
    # two-hop route that hides the PART_OF/PARTNERS_WITH path someone
    # actually asked for.
    excluded_from_paths: true
    description: The organization's home country.
    guidance: >-
      Where headquartered or incorporated, or -- for a government body --
      the state whose organ it is. ONE per organization: assert the home
      country, not every country it sells into, ships to under export
      license, or is investigated by. If an article names a local entity
      ("Google DeepMind" vs. its Alphabet parent's other national units),
      assert BASED_IN about the entity actually named and let PART_OF carry
      it upward.
    example: Mistral AI --BASED_IN--> France

  WORKS_FOR:
    domain: [Person]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: Employment or formal service affiliation.
    example: Jack Clark --WORKS_FOR--> Anthropic

  MANAGES:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Product]
    description: >-
      The organization holds administrative/operational lead responsibility
      for a large named initiative, distinct from having built it or merely
      funded it.
    guidance: >-
      Reserve for named megaprojects and initiatives, not routine model
      releases -- most organization-to-product relationships are PRODUCES.
      Use MANAGES only when the article distinguishes an operating lead from
      its funders (FUNDS) and partners (PARTNERS_WITH), as with Stargate:
      OpenAI leads it, SoftBank and MGX fund it, Oracle partners on it.
    example: OpenAI --MANAGES--> Stargate

  PRODUCES:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg]
    range: [Product]
    description: The organization builds the product.
    guidance: >-
      ResearchOrg is in the domain because nonprofit labs and evaluators
      demonstrably ship named artifacts -- Ai2 built OLMo, METR built
      HCAST/RE-Bench -- and ResearchOrg already sits in IMPLEMENTS and
      EVALUATES, so this is consistency, not a widening.
    example: Nvidia --PRODUCES--> Nvidia Rubin

  ADOPTS:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody, ResearchOrg, Product]
    range: [Product, Technology]
    description: >-
      The subject takes up the object as a customer, integrator, or
      dependency, without having built or technically extended it.
    guidance: >-
      Product is in the domain because artifacts adopt other artifacts as
      dependencies in this domain's press -- "Cursor runs on Claude,"
      "GitHub Copilot added GPT-5.6 as a model option." Distinct from
      PARTNERS_WITH (a joint agreement between organizations) and BUILDS_ON
      (a technical lineage/derivation claim): adopting a vendor's model is
      not extending it.
    example: BMW --ADOPTS--> Figure

  COMPETES_WITH:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, Product, Country]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, Product, Country]
    symmetric: true
    description: The two entities compete in the same market or capability race.
    guidance: >-
      Product is in domain/range because this domain's press routinely
      pits artifacts against each other independent of their makers --
      "Gemini 3 vs. GPT-5.6," "AMD Instinct vs. Nvidia Blackwell" -- not
      only the companies behind them. Country is included for the
      US-China(-EU) framing that is a daily fixture of this beat in a way
      it is not in most domains.
    example: AMD Instinct MI-series --COMPETES_WITH--> Nvidia Blackwell

  BUILDS_ON:
    domain: [Product, Technology]
    range: [Product, Technology]
    description: >-
      The subject is a technical extension, distillation, fine-tune, or
      direct successor of the object.
    guidance: >-
      Covers both artifact lineage (DeepSeek's R-series distilled from
      DeepSeek V3-lineage checkpoints; Google's Antigravity coding platform
      built on Gemini 3) and technique lineage (GRPO, popularized by
      DeepSeek's R1 paper, as a cheaper alternative built on the PPO
      approach). Not for "uses as a vendor dependency" -- that is ADOPTS.
    example: GRPO --BUILDS_ON--> PPO

  IMPLEMENTS:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, Product]
    range: [Technology]
    description: The subject employs this technique or architecture.
    guidance: >-
      Company and ResearchOrg are included alongside Product because this
      domain's press often attributes a technique to the lab directly
      ("Anthropic uses Constitutional AI to train Claude") rather than to
      the shipped model. Use Product when the claim is about the artifact
      specifically ("DeepSeek V4 is a MoE model").
    example: DeepSeek V4 --IMPLEMENTS--> Mixture of Experts

  FUNDS:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, Product]
    description: The subject provides capital to the object.
    guidance: >-
      Range includes Product for megaproject-level financing that targets a
      named initiative rather than the operating company outright, as with
      Stargate's sovereign-fund backers. Use PARTNERS_WITH, not FUNDS, for
      compute-supply or reselling deals with no direct capital investment.
    example: SoftBank Group --FUNDS--> OpenAI

  PARTNERS_WITH:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody, Country]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody, Country]
    symmetric: true
    description: >-
      A teaming, reselling, compute-supply, or bilateral cooperation
      agreement.
    guidance: >-
      Symmetric: store once, do not also assert the reverse. Country is
      included for state-to-state AI cooperation agreements (a national
      AI-safety-summit declaration, a bilateral compute or research pact),
      distinct from REGULATES, which is one-directional authority rather
      than a mutual agreement.
    example: Microsoft --PARTNERS_WITH--> OpenAI

  REGULATES:
    domain: [GovernmentBody, Country]
    range: [Company, Product, Technology, Country]
    description: >-
      The subject sets binding rules for, approves, or restricts the
      object's operation or availability.
    guidance: >-
      Covers approval gating (the CAC's generative-AI service approval that
      every Chinese lab must clear before public release), enforcement (the
      European AI Office's general-purpose-AI obligations), and export
      restriction, where the object is the country whose access is
      restricted -- "the US restricts advanced chip exports to China" is
      REGULATES with a Country object, which is why Country is in range as
      well as domain. Country is in the domain because this beat routinely
      attributes restriction to the state rather than a named agency; prefer
      the specific GovernmentBody when the article names one.
    example: Cyberspace Administration of China --REGULATES--> DeepSeek

  ACQUIRED:
    domain: [Company]
    range: [Company]
    description: The subject acquired the object.
    guidance: >-
      Acquirer --ACQUIRED--> acquired. Also use for large-scale acquihire /
      technology-licensing deals functionally equivalent to an acquisition
      (Nvidia's ~$20B deal for Groq's LPU design team and technology), since
      this domain's press does not consistently distinguish the two and the
      weaker reading ("licensed") would understate deals reported as
      effectively buying the team.
    example: Nvidia --ACQUIRED--> Groq

  LEADS:
    domain: [Person]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: The person has named leadership responsibility.
    example: Ilya Sutskever --LEADS--> Safe Superintelligence Inc.

  EVALUATES:
    domain: [ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Product]
    description: >-
      The subject formally tests the object for capability, safety, or
      security properties.
    guidance: >-
      For third-party evaluators and safety institutes (METR, Apollo
      Research, UK AI Security Institute) testing a lab's product, as
      distinct from the lab's own internal red-teaming, which is not
      asserted as a relation between two entities.
    example: Apollo Research --EVALUATES--> ChatGPT (GPT-5.6)

  BENCHMARKED_ON:
    domain: [Product]
    range: [Product]
    description: >-
      The subject's performance is measured against this named benchmark.
    guidance: >-
      Object should generally be a Product with product_type benchmark
      (SWE-bench, MMLU, ARC-AGI, Chatbot Arena); the type system does not
      enforce the subtype, so this is a modeling convention rather than a
      hard constraint. Distinct from EVALUATES, whose subject is an
      evaluator organization running a formal process, not a leaderboard
      score.
    example: Claude Code --BENCHMARKED_ON--> SWE-bench (Verified)

# ── rewrites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Ill-typed shapes the model reaches for with exactly one safe rendering.
# Applied before the domain/range check; the fact is stamped
# `method='extraction_rewritten'` instead of dropped. Every `when` must be
# ill-typed today, every `then` well-typed -- the loader enforces both,
# which also makes the table acyclic.

rewrites:
  - when: { predicate: PART_OF, subject: [Product], object: [Company, ResearchOrg] }
    then: { predicate: PRODUCES, swap: true }
    note: >-
      "Claude Code is part of Anthropic's product line" is ordinary English
      naming the wrong edge; PART_OF's domain/range excludes Product on
      both sides on purpose, because a product inside the recursive org
      chart would make "what is X part of" return two incompatible kinds of
      answer. Anthropic --PRODUCES--> Claude Code is the same fact inverted.
  - when: { predicate: PART_OF, subject: [Product], object: [Product] }
    then: { predicate: BUILDS_ON }
    note: >-
      "Sora is part of the ChatGPT product suite" reads as composition, not
      an org-chart claim; BUILDS_ON is the artifact-lineage predicate and
      needs no direction change since both predicates put the derived/child
      thing first.
  - when:
      predicate: PART_OF
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Country]
    then: { predicate: BASED_IN }
    note: >-
      The common miss named in PART_OF's own guidance: an organization is
      BASED_IN its country, never PART_OF it. Countries are never a PART_OF
      object.
  - when: { predicate: PRODUCES, subject: [Company, ResearchOrg], object: [Technology] }
    then: { predicate: IMPLEMENTS }
    note: >-
      Strictly weaker: "builds" becomes "employs this technique," which an
      organization credited with producing a technology necessarily does,
      without claiming exclusive authorship the way PRODUCES would for a
      Product.
  - when:
      predicate: LEADS
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Person]
    then: { predicate: LEADS, swap: true }
    note: >-
      Pure inversion -- LEADS' subject is always the Person. The subject
      list here is LEADS.range spelled out, so the rewritten triple is
      legal by construction.

# Infrastructure edges. Written by the projector, never asserted by the model.
internal_predicates:
  MENTIONS:    { from: Article, to: Entity }
  FROM_SOURCE: { from: Article, to: Source }
  FEATURED_IN: { from: Article, to: Brief }

#
# Generated file: the model's schema enums, the analyze extraction guide, the
# writer's predicate whitelist, the projector's filter, docs/graph-schema.md

# A data file rather than code because an enum enforces MEMBERSHIP but not

# ── the organisation family ──────────────────────────────────────────

# funds it," "who studies / evaluates it," and "who regulates / convenes it"
# as different actors with different verbs -- a lab COMPETES_FOR nothing a
# regulator does, and a regulator REGULATES nothing a lab does. Splitting them
# is what makes "which companies compete with each other" and "which bodies
# regulate this model" separately queryable instead of both landing on one
# 400-entity bucket.

entity_types:
  Company:
    # color_slot indexes the --entity-slot-* palette; unique per type, 1..9.
    color_slot: 1
    prefix: company
    description: >-
      A commercial firm in the AI stack: a frontier lab, chipmaker, foundry,
      hyperscaler cloud, AI-native startup, or an investor funding any of
      those.
    guidance: >-
      Anything that sells, ships, or funds AI products -- including labs
      whose charter is nonprofit-adjacent (OpenAI's nonprofit-controlled
      capped-profit structure, Anthropic's PBC-plus-Trust structure) but that
      ship through a commercial operating entity: file the entity acting in
      the sentence as the Company, and reserve ResearchOrg for when an
      article is specifically about the nonprofit/governance side rather than
      the product. A renamed or restructured division is its own Company
      linked with PART_OF ("Meta Superintelligence Labs" is not "Meta AI"
      once the article treats the restructuring as real). Sovereign wealth
      vehicles (MGX, PIF, Mubadala) are Companies with org_type investor, not
      GovernmentBodies -- they write cheques and sit in cap tables the way
      Sequoia does, which is how the press treats them even though the money
      is state-owned. A single-product startup named identically to its
      product (Perplexity, Midjourney, Runway, DeepSeek) is the Company; the
      product of the same name is a Product -- see confusable_with.
    examples: [OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, TSMC, DeepSeek, Mistral AI, Thrive Capital, SoftBank Group]
    org_types: [lab, hyperscaler, chipmaker, foundry, startup, investor]
    # Perplexity, Midjourney, Runway and DeepSeek are all cases where the
    # company and its (only) product share one name with no textual signal
    # distinguishing "Perplexity raised a round" from "Perplexity shipped a
    # feature." NOT confusable with GovernmentBody: sovereign-fund status is
    # settled by fiat above (org_type: investor), not by an ambiguous
    # sentence, so there is no real blur to name there.
    confusable_with: [ResearchOrg, Product]

  GovernmentBody:
    color_slot: 2
    prefix: govt
    description: >-
      A state, intergovernmental, or standards arm with staff and a mandate
      to regulate, evaluate, approve, or fund AI on behalf of a public
      authority.
    guidance: >-
      Anything that approves, restricts, standardizes, or evaluates on
      government authority. Use the most specific body named -- "UK AI
      Security Institute," not "the UK government." A named coalition with a
      governing process but no shared staff (the International AI Safety
      Institute Network, launched from the Bletchley Summit process) still
      belongs here, the way NATO does in an alliance-heavy domain: connect
      its member institutes with PART_OF rather than inventing a membership
      predicate. The EU is a GovernmentBody (the European AI Office is its
      organ) even though "the US-China-EU AI race" is common framing --
      assert REGULATES or COMPETES_WITH about the body or country actually
      named in the sentence, not "Europe" generically.
    examples: [Cyberspace Administration of China, European AI Office, UK AI Security Institute, US FTC, NIST/CAISI, OECD.AI Policy Observatory]
    org_types: [regulator, standards_body, evaluator_institute, coalition, agency]
    confusable_with: []

  ResearchOrg:
    color_slot: 3
    prefix: research
    description: >-
      A body that studies, evaluates, or publishes open research rather than
      selling or regulating: a nonprofit lab, academic institute, third-party
      evaluator, or open-research collective.
    guidance: >-
      Non-commercial by construction, even when it ships models or holds
      paid contracts -- Ai2 publishing OLMo, or METR running commissioned
      evaluations, does not make either a Company, the same way an FFRDC
      holding a contract doesn't make it a prime. Use ResearchOrg for a
      frontier lab's nonprofit or research-only face specifically when the
      article is about governance rather than product (OpenAI's controlling
      nonprofit foundation, as distinct from OpenAI Global LLC the Company).
    examples: [METR, Epoch AI, Apollo Research, Allen Institute for AI, Stanford HAI, Mila, EleutherAI, MIRI]
    org_types: [nonprofit_lab, academic, evaluator, open_collective, think_tank]
    # Intergovernmental policy arms (OECD.AI) and government-adjacent
    # standards evaluators (NIST/CAISI, UK AISI) sit on a real boundary: is
    # a "policy observatory" GovernmentBody staff or ResearchOrg-style
    # analysis? The sentence rarely settles it, unlike the settled
    # Company/GovernmentBody question above.
    confusable_with: [GovernmentBody]

# NOT an entity: a PUBLISHER (TechCrunch, The Information, Import AI) is
# `documents.source_id` and becomes an entity only when an article is ABOUT
# the publication itself. An EVENT -- even a named recurring one like the
# Bletchley/Seoul/Paris AI Action Summit series -- has no single stable
# canonical surface across write-ups ("the Paris summit," "AI Action Summit
# 2025," "the third safety summit") and no relation in this file needs it as
# an endpoint; a claim ABOUT a summit is really a claim about the
# GovernmentBodies or Countries that attended or issued a declaration there.

  Product:
    color_slot: 4
    prefix: product
    description: >-
      A specific, named AI artifact someone builds: a model, a chip, a
      coding agent, an agent platform, a robot, or a benchmark.
    guidance: >-
      Concrete and nameable, with a canonical surface independent of who
      currently owns it. A model FAMILY name (Claude, Gemini 3, Llama 4) is
      the Product, not each numbered checkpoint or point release -- track
      version strings as an attribute of the assertion, not a new entity.
      Chips (Nvidia Rubin, TPU Ironwood), coding agents (Claude Code,
      Cursor, GitHub Copilot), enterprise agent platforms (Salesforce
      Agentforce, Palantir AIP, Amazon Bedrock), robots (Figure, Tesla
      Optimus), and benchmarks (SWE-bench, MMLU, ARC-AGI, Chatbot Arena) are
      all Products; product_type carries the distinction, the way
      platform_type would in a hardware-only domain. A named megaproject
      with sponsors and sites (Stargate) is a Product too, product_type
      infra_project -- it is a thing being built, not the org building it.
    examples: [Claude, ChatGPT (GPT-5.6), Gemini 3, Nvidia Rubin, Claude Code, Figure, SWE-bench (Verified), Stargate]
    product_types: [model, chip, software_platform, coding_agent, agent_platform, robot, benchmark, infra_project, media_tool]
    # A named technique/architecture (Technology) and the flagship product
    # that popularizes it sit on one boundary the sentence rarely settles --
    # is "MCP" the protocol (Technology) or the thing Anthropic shipped
    # (Product)? See Technology.confusable_with for the declaration.
    confusable_with: [Technology]

  Technology:
    color_slot: 5
    prefix: tech
    description: >-
      A capability, architecture, or training technique independent of who
      ships it.
    guidance: >-
      Use for methods and architectures, not the named artifact that
      implements them -- "mixture of experts" is a Technology; "DeepSeek V4"
      is a Product that IMPLEMENTS it. Training/alignment techniques (RLHF,
      DPO, GRPO, Constitutional AI), architectural patterns (MoE,
      retrieval-augmented generation, test-time compute), and research
      capability areas (interpretability, red-teaming) belong here, not as
      Products, even when a lab brands its version with a product-sounding
      name (Anthropic's "Constitutional AI").
    examples: [Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, Mixture of Experts, test-time compute, Constitutional AI, interpretability]
    confusable_with: []

  Person:
    color_slot: 6
    prefix: person
    description: A named individual in a professional AI-industry capacity.
    guidance: >-
      Only extract people whose role matters to the relationship being
      asserted -- a founder, a researcher who moved labs, a named executive
      -- not a quoted bystander. Several flagship model names double as
      ordinary first names (Claude) or as historical figures behind chip
      codenames (Grace Hopper behind Nvidia's "Grace"); these are different
      entities that happen to share a string with a Product, not the same
      thing filed twice, and confusable_with is deliberately empty here for
      exactly that reason -- see Product's guidance.
    examples: [Sam Altman, Jack Clark, Ilya Sutskever, Demis Hassabis]
    confusable_with: []

  Country:
    color_slot: 7
    prefix: country
    description: >-
      A sovereign state -- the top-level actor an organization belongs to,
      or a party to a geopolitical AI claim in its own right.
    guidance: >-
      States only. Not blocs: the EU is a GovernmentBody (see above), and
      export-control and "AI race" coverage that says "the US" or "China"
      without naming a specific agency should be asserted about the Country
      directly -- REGULATES and COMPETES_WITH both admit Country for exactly
      this framing, which is routine in this domain's press ("the US
      restricts advanced chip exports to China") in a way it rarely is
      elsewhere. Not regions ("the Gulf") or cities. An organization is
      BASED_IN its country, never PART_OF it.
    examples: [United States, China, France, United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates]
    confusable_with: []

predicates:
  # ── archetype coverage ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # adoption/use : org|Product --ADOPTS--> Product|Technology
  # competition  : Company|ResearchOrg|Product|Country --COMPETES_WITH--> same (symmetric)
  # composition  : Product|Technology --BUILDS_ON--> Product|Technology ;
  #                Company|ResearchOrg|Product --IMPLEMENTS--> Technology
  # funding      : Company|GovernmentBody --FUNDS--> Company|Product
  # production   : Company|ResearchOrg --PRODUCES--> Product        (anchor)
  # partnership  : org|Country --PARTNERS_WITH--> org|Country (symmetric)
  # regulation   : GovernmentBody|Country --REGULATES--> Company|Product|Technology|Country
  # membership   : GovernmentBody --PART_OF--> GovernmentBody (coalition),
  #                the same recursive edge that carries corporate/research
  #                hierarchy -- no separate MEMBER_OF, matching how the
  #                alliance case is handled in the exemplar domain.
  # COMPETES_FOR (bidding for a named Program) is dropped: this domain has no
  # Program-type entity -- AI-era "competing for" claims are market
  # competition (COMPETES_WITH) or adoption (ADOPTS: a customer choosing a
  # vendor), both already expressible, not bids against a named acquisition
  # effort the way defense-press COMPETES_FOR claims are.

  PART_OF:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: The subject is a constituent part of the object.
    guidance: >-
      Child --PART_OF--> parent, always. This is the recursive org chart:
      Meta Superintelligence Labs PART_OF Meta once a restructuring is
      treated as real by the article; UK AI Security Institute PART_OF the
      International AI Safety Institute Network, the way NATO's members
      connect to NATO. It crosses the three org types freely by design. A
      Product is never PART_OF anything and this is the commonest miss --
      "Claude Code is part of Anthropic's product line" is ordinary English
      naming the wrong edge; the org PRODUCES the product, and the loader
      rewrites this shape rather than dropping it (see rewrites). Countries
      are never a PART_OF object either -- an organization is BASED_IN its
      country.
    example: UK AI Security Institute --PART_OF--> International AI Safety Institute Network

  BASED_IN:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Country]
    # Small closed set (ISO-backed) that nearly every org in the graph
    # points at; leaving it in shortest-path search turns "how does Mistral
    # relate to DeepSeek" into "both BASED_IN a country," a true but useless
    # two-hop route that hides the PART_OF/PARTNERS_WITH path someone
    # actually asked for.
    excluded_from_paths: true
    description: The organization's home country.
    guidance: >-
      Where headquartered or incorporated, or -- for a government body --
      the state whose organ it is. ONE per organization: assert the home
      country, not every country it sells into, ships to under export
      license, or is investigated by. If an article names a local entity
      ("Google DeepMind" vs. its Alphabet parent's other national units),
      assert BASED_IN about the entity actually named and let PART_OF carry
      it upward.
    example: Mistral AI --BASED_IN--> France

  WORKS_FOR:
    domain: [Person]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: Employment or formal service affiliation.
    example: Jack Clark --WORKS_FOR--> Anthropic

  MANAGES:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Product]
    description: >-
      The organization holds administrative/operational lead responsibility
      for a large named initiative, distinct from having built it or merely
      funded it.
    guidance: >-
      Reserve for named megaprojects and initiatives, not routine model
      releases -- most organization-to-product relationships are PRODUCES.
      Use MANAGES only when the article distinguishes an operating lead from
      its funders (FUNDS) and partners (PARTNERS_WITH), as with Stargate:
      OpenAI leads it, SoftBank and MGX fund it, Oracle partners on it.
    example: OpenAI --MANAGES--> Stargate

  PRODUCES:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg]
    range: [Product]
    description: The organization builds the product.
    guidance: >-
      ResearchOrg is in the domain because nonprofit labs and evaluators
      demonstrably ship named artifacts -- Ai2 built OLMo, METR built
      HCAST/RE-Bench -- and ResearchOrg already sits in IMPLEMENTS and
      EVALUATES, so this is consistency, not a widening.
    example: Nvidia --PRODUCES--> Nvidia Rubin

  ADOPTS:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody, ResearchOrg, Product]
    range: [Product, Technology]
    description: >-
      The subject takes up the object as a customer, integrator, or
      dependency, without having built or technically extended it.
    guidance: >-
      Product is in the domain because artifacts adopt other artifacts as
      dependencies in this domain's press -- "Cursor runs on Claude,"
      "GitHub Copilot added GPT-5.6 as a model option." Distinct from
      PARTNERS_WITH (a joint agreement between organizations) and BUILDS_ON
      (a technical lineage/derivation claim): adopting a vendor's model is
      not extending it.
    example: BMW --ADOPTS--> Figure

  COMPETES_WITH:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, Product, Country]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, Product, Country]
    symmetric: true
    description: The two entities compete in the same market or capability race.
    guidance: >-
      Product is in domain/range because this domain's press routinely
      pits artifacts against each other independent of their makers --
      "Gemini 3 vs. GPT-5.6," "AMD Instinct vs. Nvidia Blackwell" -- not
      only the companies behind them. Country is included for the
      US-China(-EU) framing that is a daily fixture of this beat in a way
      it is not in most domains.
    example: AMD Instinct MI-series --COMPETES_WITH--> Nvidia Blackwell

  BUILDS_ON:
    domain: [Product, Technology]
    range: [Product, Technology]
    description: >-
      The subject is a technical extension, distillation, fine-tune, or
      direct successor of the object.
    guidance: >-
      Covers both artifact lineage (DeepSeek's R-series distilled from
      DeepSeek V3-lineage checkpoints; Google's Antigravity coding platform
      built on Gemini 3) and technique lineage (GRPO, popularized by
      DeepSeek's R1 paper, as a cheaper alternative built on the PPO
      approach). Not for "uses as a vendor dependency" -- that is ADOPTS.
    example: GRPO --BUILDS_ON--> PPO

  IMPLEMENTS:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, Product]
    range: [Technology]
    description: The subject employs this technique or architecture.
    guidance: >-
      Company and ResearchOrg are included alongside Product because this
      domain's press often attributes a technique to the lab directly
      ("Anthropic uses Constitutional AI to train Claude") rather than to
      the shipped model. Use Product when the claim is about the artifact
      specifically ("DeepSeek V4 is a MoE model").
    example: DeepSeek V4 --IMPLEMENTS--> Mixture of Experts

  FUNDS:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, Product]
    description: The subject provides capital to the object.
    guidance: >-
      Range includes Product for megaproject-level financing that targets a
      named initiative rather than the operating company outright, as with
      Stargate's sovereign-fund backers. Use PARTNERS_WITH, not FUNDS, for
      compute-supply or reselling deals with no direct capital investment.
    example: SoftBank Group --FUNDS--> OpenAI

  PARTNERS_WITH:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody, Country]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody, Country]
    symmetric: true
    description: >-
      A teaming, reselling, compute-supply, or bilateral cooperation
      agreement.
    guidance: >-
      Symmetric: store once, do not also assert the reverse. Country is
      included for state-to-state AI cooperation agreements (a national
      AI-safety-summit declaration, a bilateral compute or research pact),
      distinct from REGULATES, which is one-directional authority rather
      than a mutual agreement.
    example: Microsoft --PARTNERS_WITH--> OpenAI

  REGULATES:
    domain: [GovernmentBody, Country]
    range: [Company, Product, Technology, Country]
    description: >-
      The subject sets binding rules for, approves, or restricts the
      object's operation or availability.
    guidance: >-
      Covers approval gating (the CAC's generative-AI service approval that
      every Chinese lab must clear before public release), enforcement (the
      European AI Office's general-purpose-AI obligations), and export
      restriction, where the object is the country whose access is
      restricted -- "the US restricts advanced chip exports to China" is
      REGULATES with a Country object, which is why Country is in range as
      well as domain. Country is in the domain because this beat routinely
      attributes restriction to the state rather than a named agency; prefer
      the specific GovernmentBody when the article names one.
    example: Cyberspace Administration of China --REGULATES--> DeepSeek

  ACQUIRED:
    domain: [Company]
    range: [Company]
    description: The subject acquired the object.
    guidance: >-
      Acquirer --ACQUIRED--> acquired. Also use for large-scale acquihire /
      technology-licensing deals functionally equivalent to an acquisition
      (Nvidia's ~$20B deal for Groq's LPU design team and technology), since
      this domain's press does not consistently distinguish the two and the
      weaker reading ("licensed") would understate deals reported as
      effectively buying the team.
    example: Nvidia --ACQUIRED--> Groq

  LEADS:
    domain: [Person]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: The person has named leadership responsibility.
    example: Ilya Sutskever --LEADS--> Safe Superintelligence Inc.

  EVALUATES:
    domain: [ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Product]
    description: >-
      The subject formally tests the object for capability, safety, or
      security properties.
    guidance: >-
      For third-party evaluators and safety institutes (METR, Apollo
      Research, UK AI Security Institute) testing a lab's product, as
      distinct from the lab's own internal red-teaming, which is not
      asserted as a relation between two entities.
    example: Apollo Research --EVALUATES--> ChatGPT (GPT-5.6)

  BENCHMARKED_ON:
    domain: [Product]
    range: [Product]
    description: >-
      The subject's performance is measured against this named benchmark.
    guidance: >-
      Object should generally be a Product with product_type benchmark
      (SWE-bench, MMLU, ARC-AGI, Chatbot Arena); the type system does not
      enforce the subtype, so this is a modeling convention rather than a
      hard constraint. Distinct from EVALUATES, whose subject is an
      evaluator organization running a formal process, not a leaderboard
      score.
    example: Claude Code --BENCHMARKED_ON--> SWE-bench (Verified)

# ── rewrites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Ill-typed shapes the model reaches for with exactly one safe rendering.
# Applied before the domain/range check; the fact is stamped
# `method='extraction_rewritten'` instead of dropped. Every `when` must be
# ill-typed today, every `then` well-typed -- the loader enforces both,
# which also makes the table acyclic.

rewrites:
  - when: { predicate: PART_OF, subject: [Product], object: [Company, ResearchOrg] }
    then: { predicate: PRODUCES, swap: true }
    note: >-
      "Claude Code is part of Anthropic's product line" is ordinary English
      naming the wrong edge; PART_OF's domain/range excludes Product on
      both sides on purpose, because a product inside the recursive org
      chart would make "what is X part of" return two incompatible kinds of
      answer. Anthropic --PRODUCES--> Claude Code is the same fact inverted.
  - when: { predicate: PART_OF, subject: [Product], object: [Product] }
    then: { predicate: BUILDS_ON }
    note: >-
      "Sora is part of the ChatGPT product suite" reads as composition, not
      an org-chart claim; BUILDS_ON is the artifact-lineage predicate and
      needs no direction change since both predicates put the derived/child
      thing first.
  - when:
      predicate: PART_OF
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Country]
    then: { predicate: BASED_IN }
    note: >-
      The common miss named in PART_OF's own guidance: an organization is
      BASED_IN its country, never PART_OF it. Countries are never a PART_OF
      object.
  - when: { predicate: PRODUCES, subject: [Company, ResearchOrg], object: [Technology] }
    then: { predicate: IMPLEMENTS }
    note: >-
      Strictly weaker: "builds" becomes "employs this technique," which an
      organization credited with producing a technology necessarily does,
      without claiming exclusive authorship the way PRODUCES would for a
      Product.
  - when:
      predicate: LEADS
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Person]
    then: { predicate: LEADS, swap: true }
    note: >-
      Pure inversion -- LEADS' subject is always the Person. The subject
      list here is LEADS.range spelled out, so the rewritten triple is
      legal by construction.

# Infrastructure edges. Written by the projector, never asserted by the model.
internal_predicates:
  MENTIONS:    { from: Article, to: Entity }
  FROM_SOURCE: { from: Article, to: Source }
  FEATURED_IN: { from: Article, to: Brief }

structured_output.document:
# venona ontology -- AI-industry instance. THE contract between research and graph.
#
# Generated file: the model's schema enums, the analyze extraction guide, the
# writer's predicate whitelist, the projector's filter, docs/graph-schema.md
# and the --entity-* tokens are all GENERATED from this. Edit here, bump
# `version`, rebuild.
#
# A data file rather than code because an enum enforces MEMBERSHIP but not
# MEANING: a whitelisted predicate used backwards ("$99M OTA AWARDED_TO
# Anduril") rots silently in a graph with no `domain`/`range` to reject it at
# load time. This file is that rejection.

version: 1

# ── the organisation family ──────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Three types, not one `Organization`. AI-industry press treats "who sells /
# funds it," "who studies / evaluates it," and "who regulates / convenes it"
# as different actors with different verbs -- a lab COMPETES_FOR nothing a
# regulator does, and a regulator REGULATES nothing a lab does. Splitting them
# is what makes "which companies compete with each other" and "which bodies
# regulate this model" separately queryable instead of both landing on one
# 400-entity bucket.

entity_types:
  Company:
    # color_slot indexes the --entity-slot-* palette; unique per type, 1..9.
    color_slot: 1
    prefix: company
    description: >-
      A commercial firm in the AI stack: a frontier lab, chipmaker, foundry,
      hyperscaler cloud, AI-native startup, or an investor funding any of
      those.
    guidance: >-
      Anything that sells, ships, or funds AI products -- including labs
      whose charter is nonprofit-adjacent (OpenAI's nonprofit-controlled
      capped-profit structure, Anthropic's PBC-plus-Trust structure) but that
      ship through a commercial operating entity: file the entity acting in
      the sentence as the Company, and reserve ResearchOrg for when an
      article is specifically about the nonprofit/governance side rather than
      the product. A renamed or restructured division is its own Company
      linked with PART_OF ("Meta Superintelligence Labs" is not "Meta AI"
      once the article treats the restructuring as real). Sovereign wealth
      vehicles (MGX, PIF, Mubadala) are Companies with org_type investor, not
      GovernmentBodies -- they write cheques and sit in cap tables the way
      Sequoia does, which is how the press treats them even though the money
      is state-owned. A single-product startup named identically to its
      product (Perplexity, Midjourney, Runway, DeepSeek) is the Company; the
      product of the same name is a Product -- see confusable_with.
    examples: [OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, TSMC, DeepSeek, Mistral AI, Thrive Capital, SoftBank Group]
    org_types: [lab, hyperscaler, chipmaker, foundry, startup, investor]
    # Perplexity, Midjourney, Runway and DeepSeek are all cases where the
    # company and its (only) product share one name with no textual signal
    # distinguishing "Perplexity raised a round" from "Perplexity shipped a
    # feature." NOT confusable with GovernmentBody: sovereign-fund status is
    # settled by fiat above (org_type: investor), not by an ambiguous
    # sentence, so there is no real blur to name there.
    confusable_with: [ResearchOrg, Product]

  GovernmentBody:
    color_slot: 2
    prefix: govt
    description: >-
      A state, intergovernmental, or standards arm with staff and a mandate
      to regulate, evaluate, approve, or fund AI on behalf of a public
      authority.
    guidance: >-
      Anything that approves, restricts, standardizes, or evaluates on
      government authority. Use the most specific body named -- "UK AI
      Security Institute," not "the UK government." A named coalition with a
      governing process but no shared staff (the International AI Safety
      Institute Network, launched from the Bletchley Summit process) still
      belongs here, the way NATO does in an alliance-heavy domain: connect
      its member institutes with PART_OF rather than inventing a membership
      predicate. The EU is a GovernmentBody (the European AI Office is its
      organ) even though "the US-China-EU AI race" is common framing --
      assert REGULATES or COMPETES_WITH about the body or country actually
      named in the sentence, not "Europe" generically.
    examples: [Cyberspace Administration of China, European AI Office, UK AI Security Institute, US FTC, NIST/CAISI, OECD.AI Policy Observatory]
    org_types: [regulator, standards_body, evaluator_institute, coalition, agency]
    confusable_with: []

  ResearchOrg:
    color_slot: 3
    prefix: research
    description: >-
      A body that studies, evaluates, or publishes open research rather than
      selling or regulating: a nonprofit lab, academic institute, third-party
      evaluator, or open-research collective.
    guidance: >-
      Non-commercial by construction, even when it ships models or holds
      paid contracts -- Ai2 publishing OLMo, or METR running commissioned
      evaluations, does not make either a Company, the same way an FFRDC
      holding a contract doesn't make it a prime. Use ResearchOrg for a
      frontier lab's nonprofit or research-only face specifically when the
      article is about governance rather than product (OpenAI's controlling
      nonprofit foundation, as distinct from OpenAI Global LLC the Company).
    examples: [METR, Epoch AI, Apollo Research, Allen Institute for AI, Stanford HAI, Mila, EleutherAI, MIRI]
    org_types: [nonprofit_lab, academic, evaluator, open_collective, think_tank]
    # Intergovernmental policy arms (OECD.AI) and government-adjacent
    # standards evaluators (NIST/CAISI, UK AISI) sit on a real boundary: is
    # a "policy observatory" GovernmentBody staff or ResearchOrg-style
    # analysis? The sentence rarely settles it, unlike the settled
    # Company/GovernmentBody question above.
    confusable_with: [GovernmentBody]

# NOT an entity: a PUBLISHER (TechCrunch, The Information, Import AI) is
# `documents.source_id` and becomes an entity only when an article is ABOUT
# the publication itself. An EVENT -- even a named recurring one like the
# Bletchley/Seoul/Paris AI Action Summit series -- has no single stable
# canonical surface across write-ups ("the Paris summit," "AI Action Summit
# 2025," "the third safety summit") and no relation in this file needs it as
# an endpoint; a claim ABOUT a summit is really a claim about the
# GovernmentBodies or Countries that attended or issued a declaration there.

  Product:
    color_slot: 4
    prefix: product
    description: >-
      A specific, named AI artifact someone builds: a model, a chip, a
      coding agent, an agent platform, a robot, or a benchmark.
    guidance: >-
      Concrete and nameable, with a canonical surface independent of who
      currently owns it. A model FAMILY name (Claude, Gemini 3, Llama 4) is
      the Product, not each numbered checkpoint or point release -- track
      version strings as an attribute of the assertion, not a new entity.
      Chips (Nvidia Rubin, TPU Ironwood), coding agents (Claude Code,
      Cursor, GitHub Copilot), enterprise agent platforms (Salesforce
      Agentforce, Palantir AIP, Amazon Bedrock), robots (Figure, Tesla
      Optimus), and benchmarks (SWE-bench, MMLU, ARC-AGI, Chatbot Arena) are
      all Products; product_type carries the distinction, the way
      platform_type would in a hardware-only domain. A named megaproject
      with sponsors and sites (Stargate) is a Product too, product_type
      infra_project -- it is a thing being built, not the org building it.
    examples: [Claude, ChatGPT (GPT-5.6), Gemini 3, Nvidia Rubin, Claude Code, Figure, SWE-bench (Verified), Stargate]
    product_types: [model, chip, software_platform, coding_agent, agent_platform, robot, benchmark, infra_project, media_tool]
    # A named technique/architecture (Technology) and the flagship product
    # that popularizes it sit on one boundary the sentence rarely settles --
    # is "MCP" the protocol (Technology) or the thing Anthropic shipped
    # (Product)? See Technology.confusable_with for the declaration.
    confusable_with: [Technology]

  Technology:
    color_slot: 5
    prefix: tech
    description: >-
      A capability, architecture, or training technique independent of who
      ships it.
    guidance: >-
      Use for methods and architectures, not the named artifact that
      implements them -- "mixture of experts" is a Technology; "DeepSeek V4"
      is a Product that IMPLEMENTS it. Training/alignment techniques (RLHF,
      DPO, GRPO, Constitutional AI), architectural patterns (MoE,
      retrieval-augmented generation, test-time compute), and research
      capability areas (interpretability, red-teaming) belong here, not as
      Products, even when a lab brands its version with a product-sounding
      name (Anthropic's "Constitutional AI").
    examples: [Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, Mixture of Experts, test-time compute, Constitutional AI, interpretability]
    confusable_with: []

  Person:
    color_slot: 6
    prefix: person
    description: A named individual in a professional AI-industry capacity.
    guidance: >-
      Only extract people whose role matters to the relationship being
      asserted -- a founder, a researcher who moved labs, a named executive
      -- not a quoted bystander. Several flagship model names double as
      ordinary first names (Claude) or as historical figures behind chip
      codenames (Grace Hopper behind Nvidia's "Grace"); these are different
      entities that happen to share a string with a Product, not the same
      thing filed twice, and confusable_with is deliberately empty here for
      exactly that reason -- see Product's guidance.
    examples: [Sam Altman, Jack Clark, Ilya Sutskever, Demis Hassabis]
    confusable_with: []

  Country:
    color_slot: 7
    prefix: country
    description: >-
      A sovereign state -- the top-level actor an organization belongs to,
      or a party to a geopolitical AI claim in its own right.
    guidance: >-
      States only. Not blocs: the EU is a GovernmentBody (see above), and
      export-control and "AI race" coverage that says "the US" or "China"
      without naming a specific agency should be asserted about the Country
      directly -- REGULATES and COMPETES_WITH both admit Country for exactly
      this framing, which is routine in this domain's press ("the US
      restricts advanced chip exports to China") in a way it rarely is
      elsewhere. Not regions ("the Gulf") or cities. An organization is
      BASED_IN its country, never PART_OF it.
    examples: [United States, China, France, United Kingdom, United Arab Emirates]
    confusable_with: []

predicates:
  # ── archetype coverage ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # adoption/use : org|Product --ADOPTS--> Product|Technology
  # competition  : Company|ResearchOrg|Product|Country --COMPETES_WITH--> same (symmetric)
  # composition  : Product|Technology --BUILDS_ON--> Product|Technology ;
  #                Company|ResearchOrg|Product --IMPLEMENTS--> Technology
  # funding      : Company|GovernmentBody --FUNDS--> Company|Product
  # production   : Company|ResearchOrg --PRODUCES--> Product        (anchor)
  # partnership  : org|Country --PARTNERS_WITH--> org|Country (symmetric)
  # regulation   : GovernmentBody|Country --REGULATES--> Company|Product|Technology|Country
  # membership   : GovernmentBody --PART_OF--> GovernmentBody (coalition),
  #                the same recursive edge that carries corporate/research
  #                hierarchy -- no separate MEMBER_OF, matching how the
  #                alliance case is handled in the exemplar domain.
  # COMPETES_FOR (bidding for a named Program) is dropped: this domain has no
  # Program-type entity -- AI-era "competing for" claims are market
  # competition (COMPETES_WITH) or adoption (ADOPTS: a customer choosing a
  # vendor), both already expressible, not bids against a named acquisition
  # effort the way defense-press COMPETES_FOR claims are.

  PART_OF:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: The subject is a constituent part of the object.
    guidance: >-
      Child --PART_OF--> parent, always. This is the recursive org chart:
      Meta Superintelligence Labs PART_OF Meta once a restructuring is
      treated as real by the article; UK AI Security Institute PART_OF the
      International AI Safety Institute Network, the way NATO's members
      connect to NATO. It crosses the three org types freely by design. A
      Product is never PART_OF anything and this is the commonest miss --
      "Claude Code is part of Anthropic's product line" is ordinary English
      naming the wrong edge; the org PRODUCES the product, and the loader
      rewrites this shape rather than dropping it (see rewrites). Countries
      are never a PART_OF object either -- an organization is BASED_IN its
      country.
    example: UK AI Security Institute --PART_OF--> International AI Safety Institute Network

  BASED_IN:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Country]
    # Small closed set (ISO-backed) that nearly every org in the graph
    # points at; leaving it in shortest-path search turns "how does Mistral
    # relate to DeepSeek" into "both BASED_IN a country," a true but useless
    # two-hop route that hides the PART_OF/PARTNERS_WITH path someone
    # actually asked for.
    excluded_from_paths: true
    description: The organization's home country.
    guidance: >-
      Where headquartered or incorporated, or -- for a government body --
      the state whose organ it is. ONE per organization: assert the home
      country, not every country it sells into, ships to under export
      license, or is investigated by. If an article names a local entity
      ("Google DeepMind" vs. its Alphabet parent's other national units),
      assert BASED_IN about the entity actually named and let PART_OF carry
      it upward.
    example: Mistral AI --BASED_IN--> France

  WORKS_FOR:
    domain: [Person]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: Employment or formal service affiliation.
    example: Jack Clark --WORKS_FOR--> Anthropic

  MANAGES:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Product]
    description: >-
      The organization holds administrative/operational lead responsibility
      for a large named initiative, distinct from having built it or merely
      funded it.
    guidance: >-
      Reserve for named megaprojects and initiatives, not routine model
      releases -- most organization-to-product relationships are PRODUCES.
      Use MANAGES only when the article distinguishes an operating lead from
      its funders (FUNDS) and partners (PARTNERS_WITH), as with Stargate:
      OpenAI leads it, SoftBank and MGX fund it, Oracle partners on it.
    example: OpenAI --MANAGES--> Stargate

  PRODUCES:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg]
    range: [Product]
    description: The organization builds the product.
    guidance: >-
      ResearchOrg is in the domain because nonprofit labs and evaluators
      demonstrably ship named artifacts -- Ai2 built OLMo, METR built
      HCAST/RE-Bench -- and ResearchOrg already sits in IMPLEMENTS and
      EVALUATES, so this is consistency, not a widening.
    example: Nvidia --PRODUCES--> Nvidia Rubin

  ADOPTS:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody, ResearchOrg, Product]
    range: [Product, Technology]
    description: >-
      The subject takes up the object as a customer, integrator, or
      dependency, without having built or technically extended it.
    guidance: >-
      Product is in the domain because artifacts adopt other artifacts as
      dependencies in this domain's press -- "Cursor runs on Claude,"
      "GitHub Copilot added GPT-5.6 as a model option." Distinct from
      PARTNERS_WITH (a joint agreement between organizations) and BUILDS_ON
      (a technical lineage/derivation claim): adopting a vendor's model is
      not extending it.
    example: BMW --ADOPTS--> Figure

  COMPETES_WITH:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, Product, Country]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, Product, Country]
    symmetric: true
    description: The two entities compete in the same market or capability race.
    guidance: >-
      Product is in domain/range because this domain's press routinely
      pits artifacts against each other independent of their makers --
      "Gemini 3 vs. GPT-5.6," "AMD Instinct vs. Nvidia Blackwell" -- not
      only the companies behind them. Country is included for the
      US-China(-EU) framing that is a daily fixture of this beat in a way
      it is not in most domains.
    example: AMD Instinct MI-series --COMPETES_WITH--> Nvidia Blackwell

  BUILDS_ON:
    domain: [Product, Technology]
    range: [Product, Technology]
    description: >-
      The subject is a technical extension, distillation, fine-tune, or
      direct successor of the object.
    guidance: >-
      Covers both artifact lineage (DeepSeek's R-series distilled from
      DeepSeek V3-lineage checkpoints; Google's Antigravity coding platform
      built on Gemini 3) and technique lineage (GRPO, popularized by
      DeepSeek's R1 paper, as a cheaper alternative built on the PPO
      approach). Not for "uses as a vendor dependency" -- that is ADOPTS.
    example: GRPO --BUILDS_ON--> PPO

  IMPLEMENTS:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, Product]
    range: [Technology]
    description: The subject employs this technique or architecture.
    guidance: >-
      Company and ResearchOrg are included alongside Product because this
      domain's press often attributes a technique to the lab directly
      ("Anthropic uses Constitutional AI to train Claude") rather than to
      the shipped model. Use Product when the claim is about the artifact
      specifically ("DeepSeek V4 is a MoE model").
    example: DeepSeek V4 --IMPLEMENTS--> Mixture of Experts

  FUNDS:
    domain: [Company, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Company, Product]
    description: The subject provides capital to the object.
    guidance: >-
      Range includes Product for megaproject-level financing that targets a
      named initiative rather than the operating company outright, as with
      Stargate's sovereign-fund backers. Use PARTNERS_WITH, not FUNDS, for
      compute-supply or reselling deals with no direct capital investment.
    example: SoftBank Group --FUNDS--> OpenAI

  PARTNERS_WITH:
    domain: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody, Country]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody, Country]
    symmetric: true
    description: >-
      A teaming, reselling, compute-supply, or bilateral cooperation
      agreement.
    guidance: >-
      Symmetric: store once, do not also assert the reverse. Country is
      included for state-to-state AI cooperation agreements (a national
      AI-safety-summit declaration, a bilateral compute or research pact),
      distinct from REGULATES, which is one-directional authority rather
      than a mutual agreement.
    example: Microsoft --PARTNERS_WITH--> OpenAI

  REGULATES:
    domain: [GovernmentBody, Country]
    range: [Company, Product, Technology, Country]
    description: >-
      The subject sets binding rules for, approves, or restricts the
      object's operation or availability.
    guidance: >-
      Covers approval gating (the CAC's generative-AI service approval that
      every Chinese lab must clear before public release), enforcement (the
      European AI Office's general-purpose-AI obligations), and export
      restriction, where the object is the country whose access is
      restricted -- "the US restricts advanced chip exports to China" is
      REGULATES with a Country object, which is why Country is in range as
      well as domain. Country is in the domain because this beat routinely
      attributes restriction to the state rather than a named agency; prefer
      the specific GovernmentBody when the article names one.
    example: Cyberspace Administration of China --REGULATES--> DeepSeek

  ACQUIRED:
    domain: [Company]
    range: [Company]
    description: The subject acquired the object.
    guidance: >-
      Acquirer --ACQUIRED--> acquired. Also use for large-scale acquihire /
      technology-licensing deals functionally equivalent to an acquisition
      (Nvidia's ~$20B deal for Groq's LPU design team and technology), since
      this domain's press does not consistently distinguish the two and the
      weaker reading ("licensed") would understate deals reported as
      effectively buying the team.
    example: Nvidia --ACQUIRED--> Groq

  LEADS:
    domain: [Person]
    range: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    description: The person has named leadership responsibility.
    example: Ilya Sutskever --LEADS--> Safe Superintelligence Inc.

  EVALUATES:
    domain: [ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
    range: [Product]
    description: >-
      The subject formally tests the object for capability, safety, or
      security properties.
    guidance: >-
      For third-party evaluators and safety institutes (METR, Apollo
      Research, UK AI Security Institute) testing a lab's product, as
      distinct from the lab's own internal red-teaming, which is not
      asserted as a relation between two entities.
    example: Apollo Research --EVALUATES--> ChatGPT (GPT-5.6)

  BENCHMARKED_ON:
    domain: [Product]
    range: [Product]
    description: >-
      The subject's performance is measured against this named benchmark.
    guidance: >-
      Object should generally be a Product with product_type benchmark
      (SWE-bench, MMLU, ARC-AGI, Chatbot Arena); the type system does not
      enforce the subtype, so this is a modeling convention rather than a
      hard constraint. Distinct from EVALUATES, whose subject is an
      evaluator organization running a formal process, not a leaderboard
      score.
    example: Claude Code --BENCHMARKED_ON--> SWE-bench (Verified)

# ── rewrites ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Ill-typed shapes the model reaches for with exactly one safe rendering.
# Applied before the domain/range check; the fact is stamped
# `method='extraction_rewritten'` instead of dropped. Every `when` must be
# ill-typed today, every `then` well-typed -- the loader enforces both,
# which also makes the table acyclic.

rewrites:
  - when: { predicate: PART_OF, subject: [Product], object: [Company, ResearchOrg] }
    then: { predicate: PRODUCES, swap: true }
    note: >-
      "Claude Code is part of Anthropic's product line" is ordinary English
      naming the wrong edge; PART_OF's domain/range excludes Product on
      both sides on purpose, because a product inside the recursive org
      chart would make "what is X part of" return two incompatible kinds of
      answer. Anthropic --PRODUCES--> Claude Code is the same fact inverted.
  - when: { predicate: PART_OF, subject: [Product], object: [Product] }
    then: { predicate: BUILDS_ON }
    note: >-
      "Sora is part of the ChatGPT product suite" reads as composition, not
      an org-chart claim; BUILDS_ON is the artifact-lineage predicate and
      needs no direction change since both predicates put the derived/child
      thing first.
  - when:
      predicate: PART_OF
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Country]
    then: { predicate: BASED_IN }
    note: >-
      The common miss named in PART_OF's own guidance: an organization is
      BASED_IN its country, never PART_OF it. Countries are never a PART_OF
      object.
  - when: { predicate: PRODUCES, subject: [Company, ResearchOrg], object: [Technology] }
    then: { predicate: IMPLEMENTS }
    note: >-
      Strictly weaker: "builds" becomes "employs this technique," which an
      organization credited with producing a technology necessarily does,
      without claiming exclusive authorship the way PRODUCES would for a
      Product.
  - when:
      predicate: LEADS
      subject: [Company, ResearchOrg, GovernmentBody]
      object: [Person]
    then: { predicate: LEADS, swap: true }
    note: >-
      Pure inversion -- LEADS' subject is always the Person. The subject
      list here is LEADS.range spelled out, so the rewritten triple is
      legal by construction.

# Infrastructure edges. Written by the projector, never asserted by the model.
internal_predicates:
  MENTIONS:    { from: Article, to: Entity }
  FROM_SOURCE: { from: Article, to: Source }
  FEATURED_IN: { from: Article, to: Brief }
